territorial_scope.description: Applies to US federal financial regulatory agencies and the regulated entities under their supervision; no extraterritorial reach is stated.

evidence.quote: Each financial regulatory agency shall establish, or identify an office, division, or department of the agency that shall serve as, an AI Innovation Lab

summary.short: Introduced bill requiring US financial regulatory agencies to create AI Innovation Labs where regulated entities may test AI projects under agency-approved alternative compliance strategies, with implementing rules due within 180 days of enactment.
summary.long: A pending introduced bill would require each financial regulatory agency to create or identify an AI Innovation Lab where regulated entities may test AI projects under approved alternative compliance strategies that waive or modify agency rules. Section 2 defines an AI test project as a financial product or service that makes substantial use of artificial intelligence. Applications must address public interest, systemic risk, anti-money laundering, national security, a termination date, size limits, a business plan and economic impact. Agencies decide within 120 days, extendable once by 120 days, after which an undecided application is deemed approved. Approved projects may face enforcement only as the strategy provides, with fraud and unsafe or unsound practices remaining actionable. Denied applicants face a 30-day enforcement delay and may resubmit at most two substantially similar applications. Agencies may seek injunctions against projects posing immediate danger or specified risks. Within 180 days of enactment, agencies must issue regulations; annual outcome reports begin two years after enactment.

notes: Registry status is pending; the document is the bill as introduced. The bill cites no enabling act and does not amend, repeal, implement or transpose any listed instrument, so all relations are definitional or jurisdictional cross-references. Several Acts appear in more than one provision (e.g., Sarbanes-Oxley in Sec. 2(2)(B)(xi) and Sec. 2(5)(C); Securities Exchange Act, Investment Company Act and Investment Advisers Act also in Sec. 2(5)); they are coded once each. Target instruments are not in the registry as far as known, so target_instrument_id is empty. No internal inconsistency was found in the cross-references checked.
